summary: No-ship: the structured Set-Cookie path can change certified legacy bytes, and the persisted/domain seams are unsafe foundations for tickets 02 and 06.
triage: review-gate SKILL.md § Triage governs: render EVERY finding as a full table row, never inside a dialog; then ask the ROUND before the rows — take every Proposed decision as it stands, or decide row by row — and `as proposed` ends the round in that ONE action; only if row-by-row was chosen, ask per finding with that row's Proposed decision as the first option, a reject or defer taking a free-text reason; echo back ONLY the rows that carried free text, and none if the round was decided by selection alone; max 2 rounds, append decisions.md and COMMIT it with this artifact.

findings.title: Parser-certified cookies can still emit different bytes
findings.body: The parser certifies a structured migration by comparing the input with `assembleSetCookie`, but compilation applies an additional empty-cookie rule that the assembler does not share. For example, legacy ` =; Path=/` round-trips through the parser as `{ name: ' ', value: '', path: '/' }`; compilation then trims the name, treats the line as empty, and—under the normal `emptyMeans: 'remove'` setting—removes Set-Cookie instead of emitting the original bytes. This disproves the central structured-path preservation claim.
findings.recommendation: Use one canonical emission function for both parser acceptance and compilation, or reject whitespace-only cookie names before accepting a structured parse. Add a public migration→compile regression test for every accepted parse, including whitespace-only names with empty values and attributes.

findings.title: The v3 cookie type persists contradictory raw and structured states
findings.body: The specification calls raw preservation a separate representation, but `SetCookieModification` instead requires structured fields and adds optional `raw`. Validation consequently accepts records containing both representations, while compilation gives `raw` absolute precedence. Ticket 06 can spread-edit and save new structured fields while retaining `raw`, report success, and continue emitting the old line. Because this ambiguity is part of persisted v3, correcting it after release may require another format boundary.
findings.recommendation: Model raw-preserved and structured cookies as mutually exclusive discriminated variants, validate exactly one representation, and expose an explicit raw-to-structured conversion that removes the raw variant.

findings.title: Imports bypass the ordered versioned migration seam ticket 02 must extend
findings.body: Semantic cookie conversion is hidden inside version-agnostic `backfillModification`. Stored-state migration materializes legacy filters before v2→v3, but imports call this backfill before `normalizeImportedProfiles` materializes those filters and never traverse `upgradeToCurrent`. Ticket 02 therefore cannot add retirement, counting, and notice creation once and obtain the same ordered behavior for storage and imports: adding it here runs too early and on current-v3 reads, while adding it elsewhere duplicates the destructive transformation and invites load/import drift.
findings.recommendation: Extract a version-aware profile migration returning transformed profiles plus impact metadata. Route stored v1/v2 data and legacy imports through the same `materialize legacy filters → v2→v3 transform → validate` seam, with an authoritative-storage/import integration fixture.

next_steps: Unify parser certification with the exact compile emission path.
Replace the ambiguous persisted cookie shape with exclusive variants before v3 ships.
Establish one ordered, version-aware profile migration seam shared by storage and imports before implementing ticket 02.
